nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Shallow, clear water lets light reach the seagrass and reef algae on the bay floor.

nodes.name: Warm clear ocean water
nodes.desc: The northern Florida Reef sits in warm subtropical water; the park protects the reef section that makes up about half its area.

nodes.name: Canal freshwater
nodes.desc: Canals that drain the Everglades send fresh water, sediment and pollutants into the bay and shift its salinity.

nodes.name: Bay nutrients
nodes.desc: Nutrients released from dead plants and animals feed seagrass, mangroves and algae again.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Break down mangrove leaf litter, dead seagrass and carcasses, returning nutrients to the bay.

nodes.name: Turtle grass
nodes.desc: The main seagrass of the bay. Its meadows shelter young fish and invertebrates, and its dead leaves supply much of the detritus.

nodes.name: Red mangrove
nodes.desc: Lines the shore with prop roots that shelter young fish, mollusks and crustaceans; its leaf litter feeds the shallows.

nodes.name: Calcareous green algae
nodes.desc: Chalky green seaweed growing on reefs and sandy flats. Grazed by parrotfish and snails.

nodes.name: West Indian manatee
nodes.desc: A slow, gentle grazer of seagrass that visits the bay. Boat strikes are a main danger.

nodes.name: Green sea turtle
nodes.desc: Adults graze seagrass in shallow water. Green sea turtles are among the marine reptiles that use the park.

nodes.name: Variegated sea urchin
nodes.desc: A small urchin of seagrass meadows that grazes turtlegrass blades.

nodes.name: Queen conch
nodes.desc: A large snail that grazes algae and seagrass films on sandy flats and meadows.

nodes.name: Stoplight parrotfish
nodes.desc: A reef grazer that scrapes algae off coral rock, helping keep corals from being smothered.

nodes.name: Pink shrimp
nodes.desc: Young shrimp use seagrass and mangrove shallows as nurseries and feed on small bottom matter.

nodes.name: Flathead grey mullet
nodes.desc: A schooling fish of shallow bays that feeds on algae and detritus; common prey of birds, dolphins and crocodiles.

nodes.name: Caribbean spiny lobster
nodes.desc: Young settle in seagrass and mangrove roots, adults shelter in reef holes. Eats snails, clams, urchins and carrion.

nodes.name: Gray snapper
nodes.desc: Hunts crabs, shrimp and small fish around mangroves, docks and grass flats.

nodes.name: Great barracuda
nodes.desc: An ambush predator of reefs and shallows; young stay in mangroves and seagrass.

nodes.name: Brown pelican
nodes.desc: A diving seabird that hunts schooling fish over the bay.

nodes.name: Osprey
nodes.desc: A fish-eating raptor that plunges for fish in the shallow bay.

nodes.name: Bull shark
nodes.desc: A shallow-water apex predator that takes bony fish, rays, turtles and dolphins.

nodes.name: American crocodile
nodes.desc: A threatened mangrove-shore predator found in Biscayne Bay; adults eat fish, crabs and small mammals.

nodes.name: Common bottlenose dolphin
nodes.desc: A resident of the bay and nearby waters that hunts fish such as mullet. Bull sharks occasionally eat dolphins.
